Painting as an Element of Mediterranean Living

Art Collection of the Villa

The interiors of the villa in Costa Paradiso are enriched by the original paintings of contemporary artist Nona Dronova, creating a unique dialogue between art, architecture and the Mediterranean landscape.

Nona Dronova is an internationally recognised artist whose creative practice combines Botanical Post-Symbolism and Expressionism. Her artistic language is based on the transformation of natural forms into emotional colour compositions, where flowers become symbols of beauty, memory and harmony.

The villa has become a living gallery where each space receives its own artistic identity through carefully selected paintings created by the artist.

Painting and Interior as One Composition

The Art of Creating Atmosphere

The artworks were chosen not only as decorative elements, but as an integral part of the architectural environment. Each room has its own emotional character, created through the relationship between colour, light, space and painting.

The Mediterranean architecture of the villa — stone, natural materials and panoramic views — becomes a dialogue with the expressive botanical world of Nona Dronova.

One of the villa's bedrooms is dedicated to a poetic world of flowers. More than fifteen original paintings create an atmosphere of delicate femininity and lyrical beauty.

The compositions feature peonies, dahlias, hostas and hydrangeas — botanical forms transformed through expressive colour. The dominant pink palette creates a feeling of warmth, softness and romantic harmony.

The room becomes a private gallery where every painting contributes to a unified floral symphony.

The main living space, combining the salon and kitchen area, is decorated with a series of large-scale paintings from the artist's Magical Garden collection.

The works celebrate the abundance and diversity of the botanical world — poppies, daffodils, lilac, mimosa, cyclamen and wildflowers gathered into dynamic compositions filled with colour, movement and energy.

These paintings transform the central living area into a contemporary floral garden, connecting the interior space with the surrounding Mediterranean nature.

The kitchen wall is decorated with a series of paintings from the artist's Millifiori collection — a name that speaks for itself: a thousand flowers gathered into a single composition.

Lilies, peonies, asters, poppies, iris, delphinium and foxgloves are layered together in dense, luminous compositions, each canvas celebrating the sheer abundance and variety of the botanical world.

Seen together along the kitchen wall, the paintings turn an everyday, functional space into a continuous, blooming garden.

The second bedroom, finished in soft turquoise and green, is decorated with large decorative panels from the series New Baroque — created in the style of ornamental botanical compositions.

Built around a sophisticated palette of deep greens, golden tones and natural organic forms, the panels weave flowers into a continuous, gilded scrollwork inspired by the rhythm of plants and the language of traditional ornament.

The paintings establish a connection between the interior design of the room and the timeless Mediterranean vocabulary of ornament, creating an atmosphere of elegance and refinement.

Welcome to the Villa in Costa Paradiso

Every stair, every wall and every room carries a painting — art and architecture woven together into a single, living Mediterranean home.
